# Oxalic acid vapour dosing

## Why vapour this year

Last December I trickled Api-Bioxal syrup over the seams. It works, but you have to open the hive in the cold and the bees take a dose by mouth. Derek Yeo lent me his vaporiser for the 2024 winter treatment and I've since bought my own. The bigger picture, counts and the summer strips are in [[Varroa mite treatment]]; this note is just the vapour, because I don't want to have to look it all up again next December.

## The kit

- Dartmoor Vapo VP-218, a pan-type vaporiser on a long handle. Bought my own in January 2025 from Derek's friend in Ashburton for £85, serial 0331
- 12 V leisure battery (the old caravan one). A car battery works too, with leads like in [[Car battery jump start]], but don't run the engine
- 3M 6000 series half mask with ABEK1 filters, changed every season
- Sealed goggles, not glasses
- Nitrile gloves under leather gloves
- Foam strip and a wet towel to seal the entrance
- Stopwatch (kitchen timer)
- Digital scales that read to 0.1 g

## The dose

Api-Bioxal powder, the licensed product (35 g sachets, £17.50 from Thorne's, batch BX-2390). Label dose for vapour: 2.3 g per brood box. I measure 2.3 g on the scales into the cold pan, never scoop by eye. A brood and a half (Primrose) gets 2.3 g plus 1.2 g.

## Timing

Broodless is the point; the vapour doesn't get into sealed cells. Checked Hazel on 21 December by lifting one frame from the edge of the nest: no sealed brood. Did all four on 28 December 2024, 11 am, 7°C, still and dry.

## Step by step

### Setting up

1. Mask, goggles, gloves on before touching anything. Stand upwind.
2. Close the open mesh floor with the insert. Varroa board in.
3. Pan cold, powder in, slide it through the entrance under the frames.
4. Seal the entrance round the handle with the wet towel.

### Heating

5. Clip leads on: red to positive, black to negative.
6. 2.5 minutes on for the VP-218. The pan glows faintly underneath at about 2 minutes.
7. Leads off. Leave the pan in for another 1 minute to cool, then out.
8. Keep the hive sealed for 10 minutes.

### Between hives

Cool the pan in the bucket of water (it hisses), dry it, reload. Each hive took about 20 minutes start to finish. Four hives, 1 hour 25 minutes.

## Safety and my mistake

On Bramble I touched the pan with my leather glove before it had cooled. Burnt through to the nitrile and gave myself a red welt on the back of two fingers. Cold water for 20 minutes, as in [[Burns first aid]], and it was fine in a week. Rule now: the pan goes straight in the water bucket, no touching.

The vapour is nasty, oxalic acid crystals reform on anything cold. Wash the vaporiser, gloves and goggles afterwards, and change clothes before going indoors. Brenda Prowse's washing line is 15 m downwind, so I asked her to bring it in.

## Results

Mite drop in the 7 days after: Hazel 412, Primrose 238, Bramble 97, Ivy 31. Recorded as VMD entry 2024-07 in the medicines book.
